title: Getting started with OncoCohortSelect
text: cohort described OncoArm object CorOncoEndpoints package, generates progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) objective response association . SimCohorts() adds binary adverse event, independent endpoints, cuts data calendar time analysis. 50 patients per cohort enrolled 12 months analyzed month 24. endpoints defined columns hold favorable direction. number endpoints can defined.
code: arms <- list(   Cohort1 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 8, orr = 0.45, resp.cor = 0.4,                                       death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 18),   Cohort2 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 6, orr = 0.30, resp.cor = 0.4,                                       death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 15)) d <- SimCohorts(nsim = 1, n = c(50, 50), arms = arms, ae.rate = c(0.35, 0.20),                 cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = 1) head(d) #>   sim   group accrual_time   pfs_tte pfs_event    os_tte os_event response ae #> 1   1 Cohort1     3.436951 20.563049         0 20.563049        0        1  0 #> 2   1 Cohort1    11.376369 10.103116         1 12.623631        0        0  1 #> 3   1 Cohort1     9.781919  1.476153         1  3.707829        1        0  0 #> 4   1 Cohort1     8.375189  5.596166         1  5.596166        1        0  0 #> 5   1 Cohort1    10.245421  3.599755         1 11.469013        1        0  1 #> 6   1 Cohort1    10.204578 10.252275         1 13.795422        0        1  1 eps <- list(   Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),   Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),   Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),   Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))

ORR P(ORR1 - ORR2 >= 0.1), PFS_HR OS_HR probabilities hazard ratios Cohort1 versus Cohort2 0.8 0.9, AE P(AE1 - AE2 <= 0.1).
code: crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),                    target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.30),                    time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA),                    cutoff = c(0.50, 0.50, NA, 0.50)) br <- BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit) br #>     group       ORR    PFS_S6    OS_S12        AE admissible        BR selected #> 1 Cohort1 0.9916396 0.8570022 0.5082659 0.3718876      FALSE 0.6330815    FALSE #> 2 Cohort2 0.5082945 0.5815179 0.7130959 0.9956593       TRUE 0.6768373     TRUE sel <- if (any(br$selected)) br$group[br$selected] else "none (no cohort is admissible)" crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),                        measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),                        target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10)) BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit_ref, reference = "Cohort2") #>     group reference       ORR    PFS_HR    OS_HR        AE admissible        BR #> 1 Cohort1   Cohort2 0.7282938 0.3353649 0.224306 0.1728606       TRUE 0.3119538

title: Comparing selection rules by simulation
text: scenario gives true parameters two cohorts: PFS OS medians, response rate adverse event rate. number simulated trials kept small vignette builds quickly; evaluation use several thousand.
code: make_arm <- function(pfs, orr, os) {   CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = pfs, orr = orr, resp.cor = 0.4,                             death.prop = 0.15, os.median = os) } scenarios <- list(   "Identical" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15),                                  Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)), ae = c(0.20, 0.20)),   "Cohort1 better" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(9, 0.50, 20),                                       Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)), ae = c(0.20, 0.20)),   "Cohort1 better, more AE" = list(arms = list(Cohort1 = make_arm(9, 0.50, 20),                                                Cohort2 = make_arm(6, 0.30, 15)),                                    ae = c(0.40, 0.20))) nsim <- 200

title: Comparing selection rules by simulation
text: benefit-risk score target values computed cohort, Cohort1 selected score exceeds Cohort2 threshold (br_diff). score Cohort1 relative Cohort2 selects Cohort1 exceeds threshold (br_ref). net treatment benefit (ntb) win ratio (wr) pairwise comparisons priority OS, PFS, response adverse event select Cohort1 exceed threshold. scenario simulated 50 patients per cohort, enrolled 12 months analyzed month 24.
code: eps <- list(   Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),   Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),   Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),   Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE)) crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),                    target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.30), time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA)) crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),                        measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),                        target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10)) res <- lapply(seq_along(scenarios), function(i) {   sc <- scenarios[[i]]   d <- SimCohorts(nsim = nsim, n = c(50, 50), arms = sc$arms, ae.rate = sc$ae,                   cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = i)   SimSelection(d, eps, crit, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2",                criteria.ref = crit_ref) }) names(res) <- names(scenarios) head(res[["Cohort1 better"]][, c("br_trt", "br_ctl", "br_ref", "ntb", "wr")]) #>      br_trt     br_ctl    br_ref    ntb       wr #> 1 0.9840167 0.28027139 0.9715141 0.3432 2.083333 #> 2 0.9974228 0.49534396 0.9086497 0.2996 1.884298 #> 3 0.6395187 0.20092152 0.6444149 0.1872 1.470352 #> 4 0.9667704 0.15834083 0.8852263 0.2728 1.761161 #> 5 0.9354467 0.85477364 0.7301443 0.1120 1.262911 #> 6 0.8789330 0.09728543 0.7966242 0.3912 2.323410

code: library(OncoCohortSelect)  arms <- list(   Cohort1 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 8, orr = 0.45, resp.cor = 0.4,                                       death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 18),   Cohort2 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 6, orr = 0.30, resp.cor = 0.4,                                       death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 15)) d <- SimCohorts(nsim = 1, n = c(50, 50), arms = arms, ae.rate = c(0.35, 0.20),                 cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = 1)  eps <- list(Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),             Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),             Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),             Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))  # benefit-risk score against target values crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),                    target = c(0.30, 0.50, 0.60, 0.30), time = c(NA, 6, 12, NA)) BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit)  # benefit-risk score of Cohort1 relative to Cohort2 crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "OS", "AE"),                        measure = c("rate", "hr", "hr", "rate"),                        target = c(0.10, 0.80, 0.90, 0.10)) BenefitRisk(d, eps, crit_ref, reference = "Cohort2")  # net treatment benefit, win ratio and win odds (priority OS, PFS, ORR, AE) WinStat(d, eps, treatment = "Cohort1", control = "Cohort2")$ci

title: Posterior benefit-risk score of cohorts — BenefitRisk
text: Components. row criteria defines component S_k: posterior probability parameter endpoint favorable (see PosteriorProb). binary endpoint parameter rate, beta prior binomial likelihood. time--event endpoint event times taken exponential, gamma prior hazard; parameter survival probability time (measure = "surv") , reference cohort, hazard ratio (measure = "hr"). Without reference cohort, component P(parameter >= target) favorable direction higher.better = TRUE endpoint P(parameter <= target) otherwise; reference cohort, probability difference reference least target (target), hazard ratio target. median can assessed survival probability target median target = 0.5. Columns criteria. endpoint (required): name endpoint     endpoints. endpoint can appear several components,     example survival probabilities two times. target (required): target value margin. measure: "rate" (binary endpoints), "surv"     "hr" (time--event endpoints); default "rate"     "surv". time: time survival probability. weight: exponent component composite score;     default 1 / K K components. cutoff: admissibility cutoff component,     NA none. prior., prior.b: parameters prior: beta     shape parameters (default 0.5 0.5), gamma shape rate     hazard (default 0.5 0). label: name component output; default     endpoint name, followed _S time survival     probabilities (example PFS_S6) _HR hazard     ratios. Composite score admissibility. benefit-risk score BR = prod(S_k ^ weight_k). equal weights summing 1 geometric mean components. score Chakraborty et al. (2026), geometric mean efficacy components times geometric mean safety components, obtained weights 1 / K_efficacy 1 / K_safety. cohort admissible every component cutoff satisfies S_k >= cutoff_k; cutoff safety component form P(Delta >= t) < p Chakraborty et al. (2026) 1 - p. Without reference cohort, admissible cohort highest score marked selected.

title: Posterior probability of a favorable value of an endpoint — PosteriorProb
text: posterior distributions given parameters. measure = "rate": rate p beta posterior     shape parameters b, example = a0 + x     b = b0 + n - x x responders among n patients     Beta(a0, b0) prior. measure = "surv": event times exponential hazard     lambda, gamma posterior shape rate     b, example = a0 + d b = b0 + T     d events total follow-time T     Gamma(a0, b0) prior. parameter survival probability     S(time) = exp(-lambda * time). measure = "hr": hazard ratio lambda / lambda_ref     two exponential models; reference group required. Without reference group (.ref b.ref NULL), result P(p >= target) P(S(time) >= target) higher.better = TRUE, P(p <= target) P(S(time) <= target) otherwise. reference group, result P(theta - theta_ref >= target) higher.better = TRUE P(theta - theta_ref <= target) otherwise, theta rate survival probability target margin (-1, 1). hazard ratio, result P(lambda / lambda_ref <= target) higher.better = TRUE (longer times favorable) P(lambda / lambda_ref >= target) otherwise. two posterior distributions independent. title: OncoCohortSelect 0.1.0
text: First version. Endpoint() defines binary time--event endpoints; number endpoints can used. PosteriorProb() BenefitRisk() compute posterior benefit-risk score Chakraborty et al. (2026) beta-binomial models rates exponential models gamma priors survival probabilities hazard ratios, target values relative reference cohort, admissibility cutoffs weights. WinStat() computes net treatment benefit, win ratio win odds prioritized endpoints scoring rule Gehan, standard errors first-order H-decomposition confidence intervals. SimCohorts() simulates cohorts correlated progression-free survival, overall survival response (CorOncoEndpoints) independent adverse event; SimSelection(), SelectionOC() CalibrateThreshold() evaluate selection rules simulation. Tests independent Python values, example Section S.4 Chakraborty et al. (2026) BuyseTest package; validation scripts inst/validation inst/reproduce.
